errors.evidence: The chart is a nested donut chart with two concentric rings, not a simple pie chart.

The chart has two rings of data. The outer ring has five segments and the inner ring has three segments. The description incorrectly flattens this structure and miscounts the total number of distinct categories.

The description completely fails to mention the primary structural feature of the chart: that it is a nested donut chart composed of an outer ring representing 'Ambiguity Std' and an inner ring representing 'Max Ambiguity'.

errors.text_span: “Std: 0.0” colored in dark blue, representing approximately 47.7% of the total
errors.evidence: The description incorrectly maps the label 'Std: 0.0' (from the outer ring, which corresponds to 38.0%) to the value 47.7% (which belongs to the 'Max: 1' slice in the inner ring).

errors.text_span: “Std: 0.47” colored in light blue, accounting for approximately 7.0%
errors.evidence: The description incorrectly maps the label 'Std: 0.47' (which corresponds to 5.0%) to the value 7.0% (which corresponds to 'Std: 0.94').
The color for the 49.0% slice is a medium-light blue, not teal.

errors.text_span: “Max Ambiguity (Inner)” colored in light gray, representing approximately 14.2%
errors.evidence: 'Max Ambiguity (Inner)' is the title of the legend for the inner ring, not a slice label. The value 14.2% corresponds to the slice labeled 'Max: 3'.

errors.text_span: “Max: 1, 2, 3” colored in light blue, representing approximately 38.0% and 39.0% respectively
errors.evidence: 'Max: 1, 2, 3' are three separate categories for the inner ring, not a single combined label. Furthermore, the percentages 38.0% and 39.0% belong to two different slices in the outer ring, not the inner ring.

errors.text_span: The slices appear to be ordered from largest to smallest in proportion
errors.evidence: The slices are not ordered by size. For example, the outer ring slices, going clockwise, are not in any discernible size order (e.g., 7.0%, 5.0%, 39.0%, 38.0%, 49.0%).
